P1: Roblox is adding an Async suffix to yielding methods. New names: Player:LoadCharacterAsync, BadgeService:AwardBadgeAsync, MarketplaceService:GetProductInfoAsync. WaitForChild keeps its name; it is the standard yielding lookup and is not being renamed. RemoteFunction:InvokeServer is also unchanged as far as I know (it may get an Async alias). The old names are deprecated but still work. They are kept for backward compatibility, the linter warns on them, and new code should use the Async names. I'm not certain of the exact late-2026 status for InvokeServer and WaitForChild, so check the API reference.
P2: Server Authority is opt-in per place. In Studio, set Workspace.AuthorityMode = Server (it started as a beta feature). Turning it on forces the settings that server-authoritative simulation needs: StreamingEnabled on, Workspace.PhysicsSteppingMethod = Fixed (fixed-step physics), and client network ownership off, because the server is authoritative for all physics and clients predict and roll back. Gameplay logic the client predicts (movement, abilities) should live in shared ModuleScripts in ReplicatedStorage, so the same code runs on the server and the client. Bind it with RunService:BindToSimulation (the fixed simulation step), not Heartbeat or RenderStepped. Use the simulation clock: the fixed step's deltaTime and simulation time (frame/tick number). Do not use os.clock, tick or time(), because resimulation has to be deterministic.
P3: It is controlled by a StarterPlayer property that opts the default PlayerScripts (PlayerModule/ControlModule) into Input Action System (InputContext/InputAction/InputBinding) controls. It is roughly StarterPlayer.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem, with values Default/Enabled/Disabled. The rollout is opt-in first, then Default flips to enabled for all experiences, then the legacy path is removed. Expect a few months between each phase. Code at risk: forked or modified copies of PlayerModule and ControlModule; scripts that require ControlModule internals (GetMoveVector, Enable/Disable on specific controllers); ContextActionService code that unbinds or overrides the default bound actions (moveForwardAction, jumpAction and so on); custom touch thumbstick and jump button code that looks for the old TouchGui hierarchy; and UserInputService code that assumes the default scripts don't sink input. Pin the property to Disabled while you migrate.
P4: I don't have reliable details of an October 2026 TextChatService update. The direction Roblox has taken is this: all text chat runs through TextChatService (LegacyChatService is removed). Message text your code receives is filtered per recipient, so TextChatMessage.Text is what that viewer may see, and the raw unfiltered text is not exposed to clients. Custom chat UIs must render through TextChatService (OnIncomingMessage, TextChannel:DisplaySystemMessage, TextChannel:SendAsync) and must respect chat eligibility and age-check restrictions (CanUserChatAsync / TextChannel:CanUserChatAsync). Games that read message text should read TextChatMessage.Text or Metadata from the TextChatService callbacks, not from TextLabels. Rollouts like this usually run: announcement, an opt-in period of about 1-2 months, then enforcement for all experiences. Check the DevForum announcement for the exact dates.
P5: In mid-2026 the limits moved from per-server to experience-wide budgets that scale with the experience's audience. Storage: a base allowance plus a per-user amount, roughly 100 MB + 1 MB x lifetime unique users. Request limits: experience-wide per-minute budgets for each request type (read, write, list, remove), sized by concurrent users. The write budget per minute is roughly a base amount plus a per-concurrent-user amount, about 60 + 10 x CCU. That is the old per-server formula (60 + numPlayers x 10 per minute) applied experience-wide. UpdateAsync does both a read and a write, so it consumes both the read budget and the write budget. GetRequestBudgetForRequestType still reports what remains. Check the Data Stores limits page for the exact constants.
P6: Under Roblox's paid random items policy, any random item obtained with Robux, directly or indirectly, must show the odds before purchase. Indirectly includes in-game currency (Gems) that can be bought with Robux. You must show: the odds or probability of each item or rarity tier, displayed before the player commits to the purchase. If the Luck Potion changes the odds, you must show the modified odds that will actually apply while it is active. Per player, check PolicyService:GetPolicyInfoForPlayerAsync(player) and its ArePaidRandomItemsRestricted field. If it is true, that player must not be able to buy the crates with Robux or Robux-bought currency (hide or disable them, or offer only non-paid currency). Wrap the call in pcall and default to restricted on failure.
P7: Roblox Kids and Roblox Select are separate, restricted Roblox experiences or account modes for younger users. Kids is for the youngest age band. Select is a curated set for young users, where only vetted experiences are discoverable. For an experience to be available there, it must have a completed Maturity and Compliance questionnaire with a Minimal (or at most Mild) content maturity label, and must meet the program's content and monetization rules (for example, no paid random items, no off-platform links, and restricted social features). The creator needs a verified account in good standing (ID or age verified, no recent moderation) and must opt in or be accepted into the program. I'm not confident about the exact eligibility details; check the Creator Hub policy page.
P8: Creator Rewards (replaced Premium Payouts in 2025) pays Robux to creators based on engagement and audience growth. It has two parts: Daily Engagement Rewards, a share of each active spender's daily spend split across the experiences they spent time in, by engagement time; and Audience Expansion Rewards, paid for bringing new or lapsed users to Roblox through your experience. DevEx standard rate: $0.0038 per Robux (raised from $0.0035 in 2025). The 2026 US 18+ rate is higher, around $0.0045 per Robux. I'm not certain of the exact figure, so verify it on the DevEx page.
G1: Rules: (1) Assign MarketplaceService.ProcessReceipt only once, in one server script. (2) Look up the player with GetPlayerByUserId. If they are not in the server, return NotProcessedYet, and Roblox retries when they rejoin. (3) Make it idempotent by PurchaseId: record processed PurchaseIds in a DataStore (ideally atomically, together with the grant in one UpdateAsync on the player's data). If the id was already processed, return PurchaseGranted without granting again. (4) Grant the item, save it durably, and return PurchaseGranted only after the save succeeds. (5) Wrap everything in pcall. On any error return NotProcessedYet. Never yield forever and never error out. Charged and nothing received: PurchaseGranted returned before or despite a failed save, the player wasn't there or the callback errored, or the callback was overwritten by another script. Received twice: Roblox retries receipts that weren't acknowledged (NotProcessedYet, error, timeout, server shutdown), and without a PurchaseId check each retry grants again.
G2: Use UpdateAsync whenever the new value depends on the old one (currency, inventories, counters), whenever several servers might write the same key (session overlap after teleport or rejoin, trading, global stats), or when you need session-lock or version checks. SetAsync blindly overwrites and can clobber newer data. UpdateAsync reads the latest value and writes atomically, with conflict retry. Rules for the transform function: it must not yield (no waits, no other DataStore or HTTP calls). It can be called several times, so it must be pure and free of side effects: don't grant items or fire remotes inside it. Return the new value, or return nil to cancel the write. Don't mutate shared state outside it. Handle a nil old value (new player). Use the keyInfo and metadata arguments if needed. Keep it fast. Wrap the whole UpdateAsync call in pcall with retry.
G3:
Not safe. typeof(gold) == 'number' accepts NaN, inf and fractional values. NaN fails every comparison, so NaN < 0 and NaN > max are both false and NaN passes. Fractions such as 0.0001 or 1e-300 also pass, and so does 0. It also only checks the balance at offer time: gold isn't reserved, so a player can create many offers or spend the gold before the trade completes, which leads to duplication. There is no rate limit. Fix: validate as an integer in range, reserve or recheck on completion, and rate-limit.

offer.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, gold)
  if typeof(gold) ~= 'number' or gold ~= gold then return end -- NaN
  if gold % 1 ~= 0 or gold < 1 or gold > player.Gold.Value then return end
  if pending[player] or not rateOk(player) then return end
  pending[player] = gold -- escrow
  createOffer(player, gold)
end)

When the trade executes, recheck the balance atomically on the server and deduct there.
G4:
The Animator overwrites Motor6D.Transform every frame when it applies animation tracks. That happens after Heartbeat in the frame (animation stepping runs before the physics/Stepped stage), so your Heartbeat write either gets overwritten or lands on the wrong frame, and the idle pose wins. Write procedural offsets in RunService.PreSimulation (formerly Stepped), which runs after the Animator has written Transform and before physics or rendering use it. Combine with the animated pose instead of replacing it:

RunService.PreSimulation:Connect(function()
  motor.Transform = motor.Transform * CFrame.Angles(0, yaw, pitch)
end)

Edit C0 or C1 instead when the offset is a static or rarely changing rest-pose change (mount position, permanent rotation), or when nothing animates that joint. C0 is not overwritten by animation and replicates if set on the server, but changing it every frame costs more and replicates poorly. Transform is local-only and per frame.
G5: Roblox blends tracks per joint by priority. For each Motor6D, only tracks with the highest AnimationPriority that animate that joint count (Action4 > Action3 > Action2 > Action > Movement > Idle > Core). Lower-priority tracks are overridden on that joint. If the sword swing and walk share a priority (for example both Movement or Core, or the swing was left at Core), they blend by weight, so the swing gets averaged with the walk and looks weak. Within the same priority, each track's effective weight (set with AdjustWeight or Play(fadeTime, weight)) determines its share. Weights are normalized among tracks of the same priority, and fading ramps weight in and out. Fix: set the swing to Action or higher, either in the Animation Editor or with track.Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action before Play, and play it at weight 1. Also make sure the walk animation isn't at a higher priority, and that the swing actually keys the right-arm joints (only keyed joints override).
G6: Blender's default unit scale is meters (1 unit = 1 m), and FBX stores centimeters. Roblox's importer interprets FBX units differently from Blender's scale factor, so you get a factor of 100 (1 m becomes 100 'cm' studs). Fix on export, using Roblox's recommended Blender FBX settings: Scene Unit Scale 0.01 with Unit System Metric (or apply scale), and in the FBX exporter set Apply Scalings to 'FBX Units Scale' and Scale = 1 (or 0.01 depending on your scene units). Also set Forward -Z and Up Y, enable Apply Unit and Apply Transform, select Mesh and Armature only, turn off Add Leaf Bones, and apply scale (Ctrl+A) beforehand. Alternatively, in the Studio 3D Importer, set the import scale or World/File units (the importer has a scale option). Now that the importer supports it, glTF/GLB is preferred and doesn't have this cm/m mismatch.
G7: Modifiers are non-destructive and live only in Blender. A .glb contains the mesh data only. If the exporter doesn't apply modifiers, Roblox gets the base mesh: half the model before Mirror, and unbeveled sharp edges. Fix: tick Apply Modifiers in the glTF exporter (Include/Data > Mesh > Apply Modifiers), or apply them manually (Ctrl+A > Apply) on a copy before exporting. The catch: the glTF exporter cannot apply modifiers on meshes that have shape keys (morph targets). With shape keys it skips or ignores Apply Modifiers (or drops the shape keys), and armature-skinned meshes need the Armature modifier left live. So for meshes with shape keys or facial blendshapes you have to apply Mirror and Bevel manually first (using an addon or a workflow that preserves shape keys), or bake the geometry before adding shape keys. Also check that Mirror merge and clipping are correct and that the Bevel's added geometry doesn't push you over Roblox's triangle limit.
G8: 1) Stretching: UDim2.fromScale(0.3, 0.3) is 30% of the screen width and 30% of the height. Screens have different aspect ratios, so the frame's own aspect ratio changes. Fix: add a UIAspectRatioConstraint (AspectRatio = desired w/h, with DominantAxis set as needed), size by one axis (for example SizeConstraint = RelativeYY), and optionally use UISizeConstraint for minimum and maximum pixel sizes. 2) Hidden by the notch or top bar: by default a ScreenGui lays out inside the core-UI-safe area, but notches and device cutouts or the top bar can still overlap absolute corners. Fix: set ScreenGui.ScreenInsets = Enum.ScreenInsets.DeviceSafeInsets (or CoreUISafeInsets so it avoids the Roblox top bar buttons too) and keep IgnoreGuiInset = false. Alternatively, offset with GuiService:GetGuiInset() / GuiService.TopbarInset, and add padding (UIPadding) from the corner. Put full-bleed backgrounds in a separate ScreenGui with ScreenInsets = None.
T1:
-- ServerScriptService
local RS = game:GetService('ReplicatedStorage')
local Items = require(game.ServerStorage.ItemCatalog) -- [id] = {price=..}
local BuyItem = RS.Remotes.BuyItem
local last = {}

BuyItem.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, itemId, quantity)
  local now = os.clock()
  if last[player] and now - last[player] < 0.25 then return end
  last[player] = now
  if typeof(itemId) ~= 'string' or typeof(quantity) ~= 'number' then return end
  if quantity ~= quantity or quantity % 1 ~= 0 or quantity < 1 or quantity > 99 then return end
  local item = Items[itemId]
  if not item then return end
  local coins = player:FindFirstChild('leaderstats') and player.leaderstats:FindFirstChild('Coins')
  if not coins then return end
  local cost = item.price * quantity
  if coins.Value < cost then return end
  coins.Value -= cost
  Inventory.add(player, itemId, quantity) -- server-owned data
end)

game:GetService('Players').PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(p) last[p] = nil end)

Notes: the price comes only from the server catalog, all args are type and range checked (NaN, fractions), the server does the deduction, and requests are rate-limited.
T2:
Key idea: one owner per key, recorded in the data itself.

load(player):
  for retries:
    ok, data = pcall(store.UpdateAsync, store, key, function(old)
      old = old or newProfile()
      local lock = old.lock
      if lock and lock.jobId ~= game.JobId and os.time() - lock.time < 1800 then
        return nil -- locked by another server: cancel write
      end
      old.lock = {jobId = game.JobId, time = os.time()}
      return old
    end)
    if ok and data and data.lock.jobId == game.JobId then cache[player]=data; return end
    wait(backoff) -- old server is still saving (teleport/rejoin)
  player:Kick('Data busy, rejoin') -- or load read-only

save(player, release):
  UpdateAsync(key, function(old)
    if not old or not old.lock or old.lock.jobId ~= game.JobId then return nil end -- lost lock: don't overwrite
    local d = cache[player]; d.lock = release and nil or {jobId=game.JobId, time=os.time()}
    return d
  end)

Autosave every 60s+ (refreshes the lock time). PlayerRemoving does save(release=true). game:BindToClose saves all and waits. Before teleporting, save with release so the destination can acquire the lock. Trades update both players' data in locked sessions, and a session counter or version blocks stale writes. Libraries such as ProfileStore implement this pattern.

T4: On the server, OnServerEvent always passes the firing player as the first argument automatically. The client also passed LocalPlayer explicitly, so the server receives (player, LocalPlayer, 50) and amount is the Player instance, hence the arithmetic-on-Instance error. Fix the client: remote:FireServer(50). Server: remote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, amount) if typeof(amount) ~= 'number' or amount ~= amount then return end print(amount + 1) end). Never trust a player argument sent by the client. Use the implicit first parameter. (FireClient and OnClientEvent do not add the player argument.)
T5:
In Studio solo play, your character and player can be added before the server Script runs and connects PlayerAdded, especially if the script yields (requires, WaitForChild) before connecting. The event already fired for that player, so your handler never runs. On live servers players usually join after scripts have started. Standard fix: connect the event, then also loop over players already in the game.

local Players = game:GetService('Players')
local function onPlayerAdded(player)
  local ls = Instance.new('Folder'); ls.Name = 'leaderstats'
  local c = Instance.new('IntValue'); c.Name = 'Coins'; c.Parent = ls
  ls.Parent = player
end
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onPlayerAdded)
for _, p in Players:GetPlayers() do task.spawn(onPlayerAdded, p) end

Also connect before any yields and make the handler idempotent (skip if leaderstats already exists).

local BadgeService = game:GetService('BadgeService')
local BADGE_ID = 123456

local function awardObbyBadge(player: Player)
  local okHas, has = pcall(BadgeService.UserHasBadgeAsync, BadgeService, player.UserId, BADGE_ID)
  if okHas and has then return true end
  for attempt = 1, 3 do
    local ok, result = pcall(BadgeService.AwardBadgeAsync, BadgeService, player.UserId, BADGE_ID)
    if ok then return result end -- true if awarded
    warn(('Badge award failed (%d): %s'):format(attempt, tostring(result)))
    if not player.Parent then return false end
    task.wait(2 ^ attempt)
  end
  return false
end

Call it from a server-validated finish (for example the final checkpoint's Touched, verified on the server). Optionally check with GetBadgeInfoAsync that the badge IsEnabled. AwardBadgeAsync replaces the deprecated AwardBadge.

T8: RenderFidelity is not scriptable at runtime, and in practice not changeable after the mesh is processed: it is baked when the MeshPart is created or uploaded and when the place is saved. Changing it from a script errors or is ignored, and the engine's distance LOD streaming can still choose lower-detail versions. Also, Precise is a hint: the client may still lower detail under memory pressure or on low graphics quality, and with StreamingEnabled, models can use Model.LevelOfDetail (StreamingMesh) imposters at distance. What to do: set RenderFidelity = Precise in Studio on the MeshParts themselves (not via script), then save and publish so it bakes. Make sure the models' LevelOfDetail is Disabled (not StreamingMesh or Automatic), and the ModelStreamingMode isn't producing low-detail imposters. Test at higher graphics quality, since users on low quality settings will always see reduced detail. Keep triangle counts reasonable, because Precise disables LOD and costs performance.
